subject: Renewal pricing — conditional anchor + short-term uplift credits
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@helioscommerce.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@helioscommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: anchor + short-term uplift

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the great work through Q2 — usage is ramping faster than we forecasted and we expect a pronounced seasonal spike in Q4 tied to our holiday campaign. We are preparing our 2028 budget and want to lock a renewal for a 12-month term starting Jan 1. Two asks from procurement:

- Can Redwood provide a conditional price anchor for 12 months (we're looking for a rate hold on the per-token price, ideally with a small commitment uplift)?
- We also need a short-term uplift credit pool (one-time or valid across two quarters) to cover our expected spike without immediate overage penalties.

If possible, send a simple term sheet or options matrix — we prefer a solution where the anchor is contingent on a modest commit increase (we can target +20% commit) and the uplift credits are capped and timeboxed.

Attached: usage_report_q2_2027.csv (internal usage breakouts).

Can we get a proposal before Aug 15?

Thanks,
Tom Nguyen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Helios Commerce

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@helioscommerce.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@helioscommerce.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: anchor + short-term uplift

Tom — really appreciate the context and the usage file. Quick take and next steps:

- We can offer a conditional 12-month price anchor if Helios increases the committed capacity by ~20% vs the current annualized run rate. The anchor would fix per-token pricing for the 12 months; overages would remain billable per normal rates unless covered by the uplift pool.
- For the spike you described, we can create a short-term uplift credit pool (proposal: $75k in credits usable across Q4 and Q1). Credits would expire after the two-quarter window and would be drawn first against overages.
- We recommend a quarterly true-up in order to avoid invoice surprises and to automatically convert sustained uplift into committed capacity on a go-forward basis.

I'll loop in Marissa from sales (pricing approval) and David from finance to finalize the exact credit sizing and any billing/proration constraints. If that sounds good I can circulate a one-page term sheet and a pricing breakdown this week.

Best,
Soojín Lee
Account Executive, North America
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@helioscommerce.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@helioscommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: anchor + short-term uplift

Tom / Soojin — looping in pricing for clarity. Thanks for the ask, Tom — we reviewed Helios's Q2 run rate and the projected Q4 bump. Suggested commercial structure (high level):

Option A — Anchor + credit pool (preferred for predictability)
- 12-month fixed anchor on per-token pricing (price hold) if Helios commits to +20% annualized committed capacity vs current ARR.
- One-time uplift credit pool: $75,000 usable across Q4 2027 and Q1 2028; credits apply before overage billing.
- Quarterly true-up and automatic conversion trigger: if average usage across two consecutive quarters exceeds the committed baseline by >10%, additional committed capacity will be converted at the anchored rate.

Option B — Smaller anchor, larger credit pool
- 8% anchor discount for current commit levels, plus a $120,000 uplift credit pool for two quarters. Lower rate lock but larger temporary cushion.

We prefer Option A since it aligns incentives for a committed expansion and keeps unit economics predictable for both sides.

Attached: Helios_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v4.pdf (one-pager). I'm happy to walk through redlines. Legal has asked for a short doc-term annex and a PO + DocuSign once commercial terms are agreed.

Marissa Cole
Head of Account Strategy
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@helioscommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: anchor + short-term uplift

Quick finance notes before we finalize language:

- Pricing floor: we can support a 12-month price hold on the anchored SKU but need to keep a documented floor to protect previously committed discounts. The term sheet will call out a floor and the mechanism for any true-up conversions.
- Uplift credits: the proposed $75k pool is acceptable, but credits will be netted against billed overages (they're not refundable). We prefer to invoice committed capacity monthly/quarterly and apply credits at invoice time.
- Billing/proration: if Helios signs a Jan 1 effective date but later elects to accelerate the commit, we'll treat the acceleration as a mid-term amendment and prorate committed credits forward.

Attached: pricing_breakdown_aug2027.xlsx (illustrative math for Option A).

If Marissa confirms Option A language, Legal can prepare a doc annex and we can send the final DocuSign link.

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@helioscommerce.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: anchor + short-term uplift

Soojín / Marissa / David — thanks all. Helios is happy to move forward with Option A (12-month anchor tied to +20% commit, $75k uplift credits across Q4 + Q1, quarterly true-up). Procurement will issue a PO as soon as we have the DocuSign link. Two quick asks:

1) Please confirm that credits will be applied to overages first and that any unused credits after Q1 will expire (we accept that).
2) Can Legal include a 90-day price-hold grace in the event of a merger or material platform acquisition? Procurement tends to request these clauses — we can accept reasonable guardrails.

We'll expect the DocuSign link and HubSpot deal update (HL-2027-0421).

Thanks,
Tom Nguyen
Head of Platform Partnerships
Helios Commerce
